comment_correction.before_comment:
/** * Cores enqueued during the current level tick, drained by {@link #end} at the end of that tick. * *

Weakly keyed: the entry normally lasts less than one tick, but a level that stops ticking * between an {@link #enqueue} and its end-of-tick drain (an aborted tick, a removed dimension, a * shutdown) would otherwise stay reachable from this static map for the rest of the JVM's life, * keeping the whole dimension with it. {@code Level} does not override equals/hashCode, so weak * keys are the same identity keys as before.

*/
comment_correction.after_comment:
/** * Cores enqueued during the current level tick, drained by {@link #end} at the end of that tick. * *

The normal handler removes the entry before exchange and reaction. Weak keys alone do not * guarantee cleanup if a level stops ticking before that drain: each value strongly holds cores, * whose level field can refer back to the key. This class currently has no unload/stop cleanup * hook, so an entry can remain if the same level never receives another end-of-tick event.

*/
comment_correction.reason: Correct a disproven weak-key cleanup guarantee; no runtime cleanup or exception behavior changed.
